standfirst: A marriage already dead on arrival, a chaebol family that treats dinner as combat, and a village of in-laws who turn out to be the only sane people in it. Park Ji-eun spends eight hours making you laugh so the second half can charge you for it. These six run the same con.

picks.why: Same writer, same architecture. Park Ji-eun's other big one: broad ensemble comedy for hours, a sprawling supporting cast who steal it, then an emotional invoice in the final stretch. The North Korean village and the Yongdu-ri in-laws serve the identical narrative function. Difference: the couple falls in love there instead of falling back in love, so it is warmer earlier.

The earliest version of the formula: a proud, absurd, deeply lonely heroine, comedy that undercuts every sincere moment, and a countdown you can see coming. Difference: 2013 production values and a much sillier premise, though the emotional beats hit the same way.

A family melodrama that is genuinely funny for hours and then extracts payment in full. Same structure of comedy as anaesthetic, and it is about the parent-child ledger that Queen of Tears keeps circling. Difference: no wealth fantasy, and the loss is not walked back.
If what wrecked you was the marriage seen across a whole lifetime, this is that idea given four seasons and no chaebol scaffolding. Difference: quieter, poorer, and it never plays anything for farce.

A terminal diagnosis inside a tight group who will not let go politely. The same weepie machinery, operated without any comedy to soften it. Difference: it does not pull back at the end. Go in knowing that.

An ensemble of adults negotiating money, family obligation and old resentment, told in chapters. Same generosity toward relatives who behave badly. Difference: no central couple and no tonal whiplash. It is sad in a straight line.

against.title: Reborn Rich
against.why: The obvious chaebol pairing. It is a cold corporate succession thriller with almost no emotional interior. The family here is a source of comedy and grief; there it is a boardroom.

against.title: The Heirs
against.why: The wealth-and-tears pick. It is a high-school melodrama with none of Park Ji-eun's comic timing, and the age gap in the concerns is enormous.

against.title: Descendants of the Sun
against.why: Suggested as the other big glossy weepie. The stakes there are external and heroic. Queen of Tears is about a marriage and a family dinner table, which is a completely different kind of dread.
